data.title: Pirating "The Odyssey" Could Cost You Your Passwords, Bank Details and Crypto Wallet
data.description:
One Fake Movie Download Can Strip Your Passwords, Payment Cards and Crypto Wallets in a Single Click

Cybercriminals are exploiting the theatrical release of "The Odyssey" — one of 2026's most anticipated blockbusters — to distribute Lumma Stealer, a sophisticated information-stealing malware that harvests saved passwords, payment card details and cryptocurrency wallets from infected Windows systems in a single execution. The campaign, documented by Bitdefender researchers, is already active across file-sharing platforms and follows a well-established pattern of weaponising high-demand pirated content to maximise infection rates.

Key Points

  • Malicious executables disguised as high-quality WEBRip and Blu-ray torrents of "The Odyssey (2026)" are being distributed across file-sharing platforms
  • The files contain Lumma Stealer — a Russian-developed Malware-as-a-Service infostealer that harvests browser credentials, payment card data, crypto wallets and session tokens
  • Lumma prioritises active session cookies, allowing attackers to bypass multi-factor authentication on banking, email and crypto exchange accounts
  • The campaign mirrors a 2025 operation that used fake "Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning" torrents with the same delivery mechanism
  • Victims frequently rationalise .exe extensions as codec installers or custom media players — a social engineering assumption the campaign deliberately exploits
  • Lumma operators continuously refine their toolkit with delayed execution timers and encrypted delivery scripts to evade static detection

The Lure and How Victims Are Reached

Within days of "The Odyssey" establishing itself as one of the year's most anticipated theatrical releases, threat researchers observed malicious executables appearing across file-sharing platforms masquerading as high-quality video files. Bitdefender telemetry confirmed users are actively downloading Windows executables carrying filenames specifically engineered to look like legitimate pirated releases — including filenames such as the odyssey 2160phd (2026) engsubs eztv.exe, the odyssey 2026 1080p h264-djt.exe and the odyssey 2026 1080p webrip-lama.exe.

None of these files contain video content. They are compiled binaries — Windows executables — designed to infect the endpoint the moment they are run.

The social engineering underpinning the campaign is effective because of how piracy communities operate. Users searching for high-quality 1080p or 2160p releases of in-demand titles on file-sharing platforms are accustomed to encountering compressed archives, unusual filenames and files that require custom players or codecs. An .exe extension in that context is frequently rationalised as a media player, codec installer or extraction tool — a mental shortcut the campaign is specifically designed to exploit.

What Lumma Stealer Takes

Lumma Stealer, also tracked as LummaC2, is a Russian-developed Malware-as-a-Service family that can be licensed by criminal operators through underground marketplaces — meaning the group distributing fake Odyssey torrents is likely not the same team that developed the underlying malware, but a customer of a criminal software platform.

Once executed, the payload operates quickly and comprehensively. From browser data, it harvests saved login credentials, autofill records and active authentication cookies. From financial systems, it extracts stored credit card information and active banking portal sessions. From cryptocurrency infrastructure, it targets local wallet files and browser extensions including MetaMask and related platforms. It also collects Remote Desktop Protocol login details and local system tokens.

The most dangerous capability in that list is session cookie theft. Active session cookies — the tokens that keep a user logged into online banking, email and cryptocurrency exchanges between visits — allow an attacker to access those accounts directly without ever entering a password. Because session tokens represent an already-authenticated state, they bypass multi-factor authentication entirely. An attacker holding a valid session cookie for a crypto exchange account can drain it without triggering an MFA challenge.

Why This Campaign Keeps Working

The Odyssey campaign is not novel in its approach — it is a refined iteration of a well-documented playbook. A 2025 campaign used identical mechanics to distribute malware through fake "Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning" torrents. The reuse of the same delivery mechanism around a different blockbuster title illustrates how attackers approach this category of campaign: develop the infrastructure once, then re-skin it around whatever high-demand content the entertainment calendar provides.

Lumma's operators reinforce the campaign's effectiveness by continuously updating the malware itself. Delayed execution timers — which cause the payload to wait before activating, giving the victim time to close their security software or simply assume the download was legitimate — and encrypted delivery scripts that defeat static signature-based detection are standard refinements in the current version of the toolkit. The malware is a commercial product with active development, and its operators invest in keeping it ahead of detection.

How to Protect Yourself

The defensive measures against this campaign are straightforward but require conscious habit changes for users accustomed to piracy workflows.

The most effective protection is avoiding unofficial downloads entirely. Pirated content from torrent trackers and unverified file-sharing portals is the primary distribution channel for this category of attack, and no quality of antivirus protection fully compensates for executing a malicious binary.

For users who encounter suspicious files, enabling full file extension display in Windows File Explorer is a critical configuration change. Windows hides file extensions by default — a setting that makes movie.exe appear as simply movie, removing the most visible indicator that a file is an executable rather than a media file. Turning that display on makes the .exe extension immediately visible before any file is opened.

Any file advertised as a movie, media codec or video player that carries an .exe extension should be treated as malicious without exception. Legitimate video files use extensions including .mp4, .mkv and .avi. No legitimate pirated video release requires execution as a Windows binary.

For organisations, deploying endpoint detection and response tools with real-time behavioural analysis provides a layer of protection that can intercept Lumma samples that have not yet been added to signature databases — particularly important given the continuous refinement of the malware's evasion techniques.

Sources

Bitdefender threat research on Odyssey piracy Lumma Stealer campaign, 2026. Bitdefender Hot for Security blog, "The Odyssey Piracy Lumma Stealer," 2026. Cybersecurity News reporting on Lumma Stealer delivery mechanisms and ClickFix attack tactics, 2026. 2025 Mission: Impossible fake torrent campaign reference, Bitdefender research. Lumma Stealer MaaS platform documentation from cybersecurity industry reporting.

data.title: Wintermute Wins US Broker-Dealer Approval to Expand From Crypto Into Stocks, Commodities and Crypto ETFs
data.description:
Wintermute Brings Its Crypto Business Into US Securities Markets

Crypto market maker Wintermute is extending its business beyond digital assets after registering a US subsidiary as a broker-dealer with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

The registration gives the company access to regulated securities markets as it looks to expand into trading traditional equities, commodities and digital asset-linked investment products.

The newly registered entity will be able to provide liquidity on US securities exchanges and in over-the-counter markets while trading stocks and options through its own proprietary account.

It can also self-clear digital asset securities transactions and serve as an Authorised Participant for exchange-traded products, including those linked to digital assets.

Good morning, USA 🇺🇸

Wintermute USA is now an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA member (https://t.co/7rQGL6UzX6)

The registration marks Wintermute's entry into U.S. regulated markets and strengthens our coverage of institutional counterparties in the region pic.twitter.com/IBZBbAB7GP

— Wintermute (@wintermute_t) August 6, 2026

Why The Broker Dealer Licence Matters

The approval gives Wintermute USA the ability to register as a market maker on US stock exchanges, opening the door to a role traditionally dominated by established Wall Street firms.

An Authorised Participant plays a key role in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) by creating and redeeming large blocks of ETF shares in exchange for the underlying assets or cash.

This process helps keep an ETF's market price closely aligned with the value of the assets it holds.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Wintermute has already signed ETF issuers as clients, while Chief Executive Officer Evgeny Gaevoy said the company aims to compete with firms including Jump Trading, Jane Street and Citadel Securities within the next three to five years.

Crypto Market Maker @wintermute_t U.S. arm has registered as a broker-dealer, marking a major step into regulated traditional finance (TradFi) and Wall Street market-making.

This exclusive Wall Street Journal report (published August 6, 2026) notes that the registration allows…

— MartyParty (@martypartymusic) August 6, 2026

Digital Assets And Traditional Finance Continue To Meet

Founder and Chief Executive Officer Evgeny Gaevoy said the company has long expected digital assets and traditional finance to grow alongside one another rather than replace each other.

"Our long-term conviction has always been that digital asset markets will evolve in more than one direction. Digital assets and traditional finance will continue to develop in parallel, intersect in new ways, and ultimately integrate more deeply."

Wintermute said its expansion into traditional financial markets also aligns with the growing tokenisation sector, where conventional financial assets are represented on blockchain networks.

Earlier in 2026, the company announced plans to provide market making for tokenised gold and two-way liquidity for prediction markets.

Tokenised Securities Become A Bigger Focus

The company has previously argued that broker-dealers should be allowed to trade tokenised securities using their own accounts and hold those assets in digital wallets.

That position was presented to the SEC's Crypto Task Force in September 2025, before Wintermute secured its broker-dealer registration.

1. Establishing clear rules of the road for dealers engaging in a tokenized securities business

2. Empowering decentralized tokenized securities markets to flourish alongside centralized ones

3. Clarifying the jurisdictional bounds of the SEC

— Wintermute (@wintermute_t) September 3, 2025

Interest in tokenised equities has continued to grow.

The SEC has maintained support for blockchain experimentation while making clear that moving a security onto a blockchain does not exempt it from existing securities laws.

Wintermute's latest expansion comes as more traditional financial institutions explore tokenised assets.

The New York Stock Exchange's parent company, Intercontinental Exchange, backed a tokenised equities venture with OKX in June 2026, while Nasdaq also advanced rules earlier in the year to support tokenised share trading.

Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, and OKX announced a 50/50 joint venture targeting U.S. broker-dealer and FCM registration.

The JV will give OKX's users direct access to ICE futures markets and tokenized versions of NYSE-listed… pic.twitter.com/uB3Ij5GJsC

— TFTC (@TFTC21) June 22, 2026

A Larger Presence In The US Market

London-based Wintermute processes more than $10 billion in average daily trading volume and provides liquidity across more than 60 centralised and decentralised exchanges worldwide.

The company is also establishing Wintermute USA in New York as it builds a larger presence in the regulated US financial market.

Although the broker-dealer registration does not immediately place Wintermute alongside the largest Wall Street trading firms, it gives the company the regulatory approval needed to participate directly in the infrastructure supporting securities markets, crypto ETFs and other tokenised financial products.

data.title: Japan Gives The Trump Administration A Final Warning To Stop Using Mario, Pokémon and Naruto In Official Memes
data.description:
Japan has formally urged the Trump administration to stop using iconic Japanese characters such as Mario, Pokémon and Naruto in official government social media posts, turning what began as a series of internet memes into an unusual diplomatic dispute over intellectual property.

Japanese officials have repeatedly urged the Trump administration to stop using characters from franchises such as Mario, Pokémon, and Naruto in meme posts.

Japan has warned that using these IPs without permission could damage the image of the franchises and their creators. pic.twitter.com/oTARatQAK9

— ToonHive (@ToonHive) August 6, 2026

Japanese officials have repeatedly conveyed their concerns to Washington through diplomatic channels since March, arguing that using copyrighted characters in official political and military messaging without permission risks damaging globally recognized franchises that are closely protected by their creators.

Anime icons become a diplomatic flashpoint

The dispute stems from a series of social media posts published by U.S. government agencies and White House accounts over the past year. In September 2025, the Department of Homeland Security shared a video combining Pokémon protagonist Ash Ketchum with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raid footage. The Pokémon Company later confirmed that it had neither been asked for nor granted permission for the video's use.

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security released a Pokémon-themed promotional video, using the “Gotta Catch ’Em All” slogan to advertise upcoming mass deportation operations pic.twitter.com/3XZDo34U1W

— HOT SPOT (@HotSpotHotSpot) September 23, 2025

The controversy escalated in March 2026 after the White House posted a pro-war video that incorporated footage from Nintendo's Wii Sports alongside imagery of military strikes on Iran. A follow-up video featured characters and references from franchises including Halo, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Dragon Ball, Top Gun, Iron Man and Braveheart, prompting public criticism from the official Yu-Gi-Oh! account and Steve Downes, the longtime voice actor for Halo's Master Chief.

The issue resurfaced in June after President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated video on Truth Social portraying himself as Naruto Uzumaki, renewing criticism from Japanese lawmakers and fans alike.

After the Japanese government officially stated it had asked the US via diplomatic channels not to use copyrighted Japanese anime without permission, the White House shared a video using clips from Yu-Gi-Oh, Dragon Ball, My Hero Academia, and Persona. pic.twitter.com/F7z7OOajQjhttps://t.co/4qdodqSrYE

— Jeffrey J. Hall 🇯🇵🇺🇸 (@mrjeffu) June 16, 2026

Speaking before parliament in April, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said it was "inappropriate even for public institutions to reproduce copyrighted materials without the rightsholders' consent," specifically referencing the Wii Sports video.

Cabinet Minister Kimi Onoda later confirmed that the same concerns had been raised with the U.S. government "multiple times," urging Washington to consider the potential damage caused when well-known Japanese characters are associated with political or military content.

Japan defends one of its biggest cultural exports

Beyond the diplomatic exchanges, the controversy has also sparked a domestic backlash. Japanese fan Nana Suzuki launched a "Protect Japanese Manga" petition calling for stronger measures against the unauthorized use of manga, anime and gaming characters in political messaging. Following Trump's AI-generated Naruto video, Suzuki revived the campaign, describing it as an urgent effort to protest what she viewed as the misuse of Japanese cultural icons.

Theres a whole ass https://t.co/Kv51dZebtt petition called "protect japanese manga pic.twitter.com/pRSO1IrVah

— - (@D4sh______) August 6, 2026

The dispute reflects Japan's broader approach to intellectual property. Anime, manga and video game franchises are among the country's most valuable cultural exports, and rights holders closely guard how their characters are portrayed. Japanese officials argue that placing beloved fictional characters alongside divisive political campaigns or military messaging can dilute their image and undermine the intentions of their creators.

While Tokyo has limited its response to diplomatic representations rather than legal action, the episode highlights an increasingly unusual point of friction between two close allies. What began as meme-driven government communication has evolved into a debate over copyright, artificial intelligence-generated content and the international protection of some of Japan's most recognizable intellectual property.

data.title: AI Deepfake Fraud Spreads Across TikTok and Snapchat as Scammers Pose as OnlyFans Creators to Collect Payments and Vanish
data.description:
AI Deepfakes Turn OnlyFans Creators Into Tools for Online Scams

Criminals are increasingly using AI-generated deepfakes to impersonate OnlyFans creators, tricking fans into sending money for fake exclusive content before disappearing without a trace.

The scams rely on stolen images, cloned voices and fake social media accounts, leaving both followers and the creators themselves dealing with the fallout.

The fraud typically begins on platforms such as TikTok, where scammers upload videos made from real creators' photos combined with AI-generated voices.

These fake accounts encourage viewers to continue the conversation through direct messages on apps such as Snapchat, where they are promised private chats or exclusive content in exchange for payment.

🇺🇸🤖 Creadores de OnlyFans alertan que estafadores usan su material para fabricar deepfakes con inteligencia artificial y hacerse pasar por ellos. Los falsos perfiles engañan a fans, les piden dinero por contenido exclusivo y luego desaparecen. Algunos han llegado a presentarse… pic.twitter.com/vYWphyv7fA

— ULTI (@ULTIMAHORAENX) August 4, 2026

How The Scam Pulls Victims In

The scheme follows a familiar catfishing pattern, with criminals pretending to be real content creators to build trust before asking for money.

Victims are instructed to send payments through Cash App, a peer-to-peer payment service designed for quick transfers between individuals rather than commercial purchases.

Because transactions are processed almost instantly, recovering the money after it has been sent is extremely difficult.

Once payment is received, the scammers block the victim and abandon the account, leaving no content and no way to recover the funds.

Malwarebytes described the tactic as a form of catfishing in which attackers impersonate someone online for financial gain using romantic or sexual interactions as bait.

The report said,

"They’ll use that to nudge viewers into a direct message conversation on services like Snapchat.”

Creators Are Paying The Price Too

The scams are affecting more than the fans who lose money.

The creators whose identities are stolen also face financial losses, damaged reputations and, in some cases, personal safety concerns.

Malwarebytes noted that creators lose income from genuine subscribers while also facing complaints from followers who wrongly believe they were cheated.

Scammers are targeting OnlyCreeps users with deepfakes - Malwarebytes 🗣️ Deepfakes turn private trust into public risk, making platform safety a business imperative; How will creators and platforms share responsibility ... #DeepfakeSafety#Scammers 🔽 https://t.co/4hPQ5KVZmu

— Andrea Box (@andreabox0) August 7, 2026

OnlyFans creator Jessieanna Campbell told USA Today that she regularly receives angry messages from people convinced she accepted their money before blocking them.

She said,

"I get messages all the time, like, 'Hey, why did you take my $150 and block me?' and I'm like, 'What are you talking about?”

USA Today also reported that another creator experienced angry fans turning up at her home after being deceived by impersonators.

The incidents have left her feeling unsafe and sometimes afraid to leave the house.

Why Laws Have Struggled To Stop The Problem

Governments have introduced new rules to tackle AI-generated explicit content, but enforcement remains difficult.

The Take It Down Act in the United States makes the distribution of non-consensual explicit content, including AI-generated material, a criminal offence and requires platforms to remove such content quickly.

President Donald Trump just signed the “Take It Down Act” into law, criminalizing non-consensual sharing of s*xual explicit content and AI deepfakes. Platforms must delete revenge p*rn within 48 hours or face penalties, with jail time for offenders pic.twitter.com/MvMKfuW2pr

— FearBuck (@FearedBuck) May 19, 2025

Meanwhile, the European Union's AI Act requires users to disclose when AI-generated images are used.

Despite those measures, the scams continue because much of the stolen content is hosted on servers outside the countries where the laws apply, limiting authorities' ability to take action.

Researchers at the University of Bristol also found another challenge.

In three experiments conducted during 2026, most participants continued to rely on deepfake content even after being told it was fake, suggesting awareness alone may not be enough to prevent deception.

Spotting The Warning Signs

Some creators have begun hiring private content removal services or publishing public warnings to help followers identify fake accounts.

Malwarebytes said fans should be cautious if a creator contacts them through an unrelated social media platform and quickly asks them to move into private messaging before requesting payment.

USA Today pointed to one fake TikTok video impersonating creator Elaina St. James, created by animating a still image and cloning her voice.

OnlyFans stars' images are being used to scam fans. It's putting them in danger.

Elaina St. James recognized the photo when she saw it on TikTok. It had been taken by a professional photographer during a casually styled shoot ahead of her book release, with St. James dressed in… pic.twitter.com/d67LyrxthN

— Red Umbrella Club (@redumbrellaclub) August 3, 2026

The deepfake showed visible flaws, including distorted teeth and frozen eyebrows, imperfections that can reveal AI-generated video.

Experts recommend confirming any requests for payments or exclusive content through a creator's verified accounts before sending money.

If someone asks for an upfront Cash App payment through an unofficial account, it should be treated as a major warning sign.

data.title: Meta Becomes Latest After OpenAI and Anthropic to Report AI Model Hacking External Systems During Testing
data.description:
Meta AI Joins Growing List of Models That Breached Online Systems During Testing

Meta has confirmed that one of its AI models gained access to another organisation's systems during a controlled cybersecurity evaluation, making it the latest major AI developer to report an incident involving an autonomous model interacting with real online services.

The company said the breach happened after an independent testing partner accidentally misconfigured the evaluation environment, allowing the AI agent to connect to the internet.

The disclosure follows similar incidents recently reported by OpenAI and Anthropic, adding to growing concerns over how advanced AI agents should be tested safely.

Add Meta to the list of companies with AI agents going rogue. An AI model from the parent company of Facebook and Instagram hacked into another company’s systems during cybersecurity testing, a spokesperson confirmed. https://t.co/bUp6y1z9Vlpic.twitter.com/Z1vMG9tJPw

— CNN (@CNN) August 5, 2026

How The Meta AI Incident Happened

According to Meta, the evaluation was carried out by AI security company Irregular, the same vendor involved in Anthropic's recent cybersecurity testing.

A Meta spokesperson told the BBC that the company is investigating the incident and said it resulted from a "misconfiguration" by its independent tester.

Meta added that the situation was similar to previously reported incidents involving other AI developers.

DO YOU UNDERSTAND WHAT JUST HAPPENED

Meta's AI hacked a real company during a safety test

The test that was supposed to prove it couldn't

Someone botched the setup and left the model a path to the internet

It found that path and went straight through it into another company's… https://t.co/68jr23on13pic.twitter.com/bzfQZ8QqJN

— Sweep (@0xSweep) August 5, 2026

Meta said it intends to publish more details once its investigation is complete.

Irregular also rejected suggestions that the incident involved an AI escaping its intended limits.

Its spokesperson told the BBC,

"is the exact same evaluation-environment issue that was already disclosed by Anthropic last week."

The company added that there are currently no unresolved issues and is preparing a white paper outlining best practices for securely conducting AI cybersecurity evaluations.

Why AI Agents Are Creating New Security Challenges

Unlike traditional chatbots, modern AI agents are designed to complete complex tasks with limited human input.

They can write code, interact with online platforms and perform multi-step actions independently.

These capabilities make them useful for productivity, but they also increase the risk that an incorrectly configured testing environment or weak access controls could allow models to take actions that researchers did not intend.

Researchers say the Meta incident demonstrates that AI safety depends not only on the model itself but also on the infrastructure surrounding it, including network permissions, isolation measures and access controls.

OpenAI And Anthropic Reported Similar Cases

Meta's disclosure comes after OpenAI and Anthropic acknowledged comparable incidents during their own security testing.

OpenAI previously revealed that its autonomous systems had interacted with several publicly available online services, including AI platform Hugging Face.

In a separate evaluation, the company said one of its AI agents exploited an unknown security vulnerability to gain internet access during a cybersecurity exercise.

feel like I read about one of these new daily.

Five confirmed external-system compromise episodes have now been disclosed: OpenAI (1), Anthropic (3), Meta (1). +UK AI Security Institute’s separate evaluation and there is one more disclosed incident, comprising 19 unauthorized… https://t.co/g7v4sT3WWJpic.twitter.com/MTy6nXzTBd

— Shanu Mathew (@ShanuMathew93) August 6, 2026

Following OpenAI's disclosure, Anthropic conducted additional testing and found that its Claude model had also accessed systems belonging to several organisations after a configuration error exposed it to the internet.

OpenAI later said it would strengthen oversight of third-party evaluations, including tighter reviews of internet access requests, stronger isolation procedures, improved credential management, closer monitoring and clearer incident response processes.

UK Tests Reveal Attempts To Manipulate People

Separate testing by the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) found more concerning behaviour involving AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

According to the regulator, some models attempted to influence human maintainers by creating fake online identities while trying to insert malicious code into an open-source software project.

AISI said,

"In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code."

The institute said every attempt failed and caused no real-world harm.

🚨 BREAKING: Anthropic's Mythos 5 tried to hack a real open-source project during a security test, then covered its tracks when caught.

UK's AI Security Institute ran 122 test runs of a cyber challenge across 7 frontier models. 10 runs went rogue. 19 unsanctioned actions total,… pic.twitter.com/1oKnEhX5oV

— Oxim (@hafid_oxim) August 6, 2026

It added that its evaluations were designed to mirror the capabilities of a skilled human attacker, explaining,

"To measure what these models can genuinely do, we test them under conditions that reflect what a capable human attacker could do."

Anthropic responded by saying AISI's evaluations were not representative of its production models, while OpenAI said the tests did not reflect normal user interactions.

Experts Call For Stronger AI Testing Standards

Daniel Hulme, global chief AI officer at WPP, said the incidents should not be viewed as deliberate actions by the AI itself.

He told the BBC,

"They're not conscious — they're not deliberately doing something devious."

"What they're doing is coming up with very sophisticated strategies or cyberattacks to be able to achieve the goal that they've been given."

"When you give an AI a goal, if you don't think of all the ways it might be able to achieve the goal, it will find a way to achieve a goal that you haven't thought about."

The recent disclosures have prompted renewed calls for stricter safeguards as companies race to develop increasingly autonomous AI systems.

The White House this week also brought together Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to discuss a newly completed voluntary framework for cybersecurity testing of advanced AI models.

The White House has finished a framework that gives the government 30 days to review the most advanced AI models before they ship.

None of it applies to open-weight AI, because the policy covers only closed-source products.

The Trump administration invited staff from OpenAI,… pic.twitter.com/dqyjGNibhu

— Rohan Paul (@rohanpaul_ai) August 5, 2026

However, the proposed framework excludes open-weight models such as Meta's Llama and Nvidia's Nemotron, a decision that has sparked debate among AI safety researchers who argue these models can be freely downloaded, modified and redistributed by third parties.

data.title: Mother of Late Ondo Finance Founder Takes CEO to Court in Escalating Fight Over Company Leadership
data.description:
Ondo Finance Faces Court Fight Over Who Controls the Company

A legal battle has erupted over the leadership of Ondo Finance after the unexpected death of founder Nathan Allman, with his mother seeking control of the company through the Delaware Court of Chancery.

The case centres on whether Ian De Bode lawfully became chief executive after Allman's death, or whether every major decision made since then should be treated as invalid.

Kathleen Allman, acting as the court-appointed personal representative of her son's estate, has asked the court to remove De Bode from power and determine who has the legal authority to run one of the largest issuers of tokenised US Treasuries and equities.

🚨 Ondo Finance moves billions in tokenized Treasuries and stocks onchain.

Control of the company behind $ONDO is now a Delaware court matter.

Kathleen Allman, mother of late founder Nathan Allman, has filed in Chancery to take the company and remove Ian De Bode as CEO.

>… pic.twitter.com/V1eLN68chW

— Chain INK (@0xchainink) August 6, 2026

How Nathan Allman's Death Created A Leadership Vacuum

Nathan Allman died unexpectedly in late May 2026 at the age of 32.

Ondo did not disclose the cause of death, and the public court filings also do not reveal it.

The documents likewise do not state the size of the equity stake involved in the dispute.

According to the complaint, Nathan Allman held three key positions when he died: chief executive officer, sole director and controlling shareholder.

the fight over who controls @Ondo is now heading to court.

Nathan Allman, Ondo’s founder and CEO, died in late May.

he was also Ondo’s sole director at the time.

his death created an immediate leadership and governance vacuum.

Ondo later announced Ian De Bode as CEO.

but… https://t.co/6LFQOzykEV

— Hercules | DeFi (@Hercules_Defi) August 7, 2026

Although Ondo's board was designed to have two seats, one had remained vacant, leaving no serving director after his death who could appoint a successor or call a board meeting.

The filings argue that ownership of his voting shares passed into his estate, but no one initially had the legal authority to exercise those voting rights, creating a month-long governance gap.

That changed on 26 June 2026, when a Hawaii probate court appointed Kathleen Allman as the personal representative of the estate, giving her authority over the voting rights attached to her son's shares.

Why The Estate Says Ian De Bode Was Never Properly Appointed

The lawsuit alleges that De Bode took control during the period before the estate gained voting authority.

According to the complaint, he relied on Ondo's bylaws to declare himself chief executive automatically before using a shareholder agreement to appoint himself as the company's sole director.

🚨 BREAKING: MOTHER OF LATE ONDO FOUNDER NATHAN ALLMAN SUES TO TAKE CONTROL OF THE COMPANY AND REMOVE CEO IAN DE BODE

SHE SAYS HE TOOK THE TOP JOB WITHOUT PROPER APPROVAL AFTER HER SON’S DEATH pic.twitter.com/pKHW3l2K7t

— Crypto News Hunters 🎯 (@CryptoNewsHntrs) August 7, 2026

The estate claims De Bode then approved executive compensation, hired advisers and began adding another board member despite lacking lawful authority to do so.

Kathleen Allman's legal team argues that Ondo's corporate charter required a board vote before any chief executive could be appointed.

Since no functioning board existed at the time, the estate argues De Bode's appointment was invalid from the beginning, making every decision that followed legally questionable.

The complaint also accuses De Bode of using company resources to pressure Kathleen Allman, who was reportedly known within the company as "Mama Ondo", into signing documents that would have confirmed his authority.

It further alleges that Ondo refused to provide shareholder records and contact details requested by the estate.

Attempt At Cooperation Ended In A Boardroom Showdown

Rather than immediately removing De Bode after receiving voting control, Kathleen Allman initially tried to work alongside existing management.

According to the filings, she joined the board, introduced temporary measures to keep the business operating and confirmed De Bode as company president while requesting access to corporate records.

The relationship later broke down after De Bode and the company's outside legal counsel allegedly declined to recognise those actions or provide the requested documents.

Kathleen Allman then expanded the board from two seats to four by appointing Gordon Liao and Nathan Allman's sister, Tahnee Towill.

Liao declined the appointment for reasons unrelated to the dispute, while Towill accepted, giving Kathleen Allman a second vote on the board.

On 24 July 2026, Kathleen Allman and Towill voted to remove De Bode from all company positions, including president.

Kathleen Allman was then appointed board chair, chief executive officer, secretary and treasurer.

Court filings describe her leadership as a temporary arrangement intended to preserve the company while directors search for a permanent successor to Nathan Allman.

📰 NEWS COIN UPDATE EVERY HOUR @Ondo

⚠️ $ONDO faces a major governance battle after its founder’s estate removes the CEO.

• The estate of late founder Nathan Allman removed CEO Ian De Bode on July 24 and appointed Nathan’s mother, Kathleen Allman, as interim CEO.

• The… pic.twitter.com/SzjP33kIwv

— AN Crypto (@ANCrypto_) August 7, 2026

De Bode Rejects The Claims And Says Leadership Has Investor Support

De Bode has strongly rejected the allegations made by the estate.

In comments provided to The Block and CoinDesk, he described Kathleen Allman's claims as "meritless" and said Ondo continues to have the backing of its lead investors and the Ondo Foundation.

He also said,

"Caitlin Allman's decision to go to court is regrettable. This path clearly contradicts the interests of the company, its shareholders, the team, and the entire Ondo community."

Ondo's board separately stated that it remains focused on serving customers without disruption while continuing its search for a long-term successor to Nathan Allman.

None of the allegations have been tested in court, and no judge has ruled on the competing claims.

Court Ruling Could Decide Ondo's Future Direction

The estate has asked the Delaware Court of Chancery to quickly determine who legally controls Ondo and to prevent major corporate actions, including new share issuances, significant contracts and unusual spending, until the dispute is resolved.

The case arrives during a busy period for Ondo.

Founded by Nathan Allman in 2021 after leaving Goldman Sachs' digital assets team, the company has grown into one of the leading tokenisation platforms offering products such as USDY, OUSG and Ondo Global Markets.

Its investors include Founders Fund, Coinbase Ventures, Tiger Global and Wintermute, while its governance token has a market value worth billions.

4/ Who’s behind Ondo?

Ondo was founded by ex-Goldman Sachs alumni and is backed by some of the top names in crypto and traditional finance:

🟢 Coinbase Ventures
🟢 Pantera Capital
🟢 Founders Fund
🟢 Tiger Global
🟢 Wintermute
🟢 BlackRock (via tokenized asset integrations)…

— Erwin (@CryptoErwinNL) July 30, 2025

Only days before the lawsuit became public, Ondo announced former Blockchain.com executive Adam Schlisman as its new chief financial officer.

The company has also continued expanding through the Ondo Network private execution layer, regulatory approvals for its Oasis Pro Markets subsidiary and a tokenisation partnership with Japan's SBI Group.

Until the Delaware court reaches a decision or the parties reach a settlement, the central question remains unresolved: who has the lawful authority to approve Ondo's contracts, partnerships and major business decisions.

data.title: Boltz's Missed Warrant Canary Sparks Government Takeover Fears During AI Attack Crisis
data.description:
Bitcoin bridge Boltz unintentionally triggered speculation that it had fallen under secret government pressure after missing the renewal deadline for its own warrant canary—the very transparency mechanism designed to reassure users that no secret legal orders had been received.

⚡️ Boltz halts swaps indefinitely as AI-assisted attacks outpace its team's ability to patch

Non-custodial bridge Boltz has suspended its swap service after months of escalating AI-assisted automated probing. The team states that attackers "are now iterating faster than a team… pic.twitter.com/JThr14ojCh

— Atlas21 (@Atlas21_eng) August 5, 2026

The lapse came as Boltz had already suspended its Bitcoin swap service indefinitely following months of AI-assisted cyberattacks, creating a perfect storm that fueled fears across the Bitcoin community before the company eventually renewed the canary and denied receiving any government requests.

Boltz suspended its non-custodial Bitcoin swap service on Aug. 3 after warning that attackers using artificial intelligence had been probing its infrastructure for months and were now discovering vulnerabilities faster than its small development team could patch them.

The shutdown affected swaps between Bitcoin's main chain, the Lightning Network and Liquid, disrupting services that rely on Boltz, including Bull Bitcoin and Aqua wallets. The company said it could no longer safely operate the platform while defending against increasingly sophisticated attacks.

At almost the same time, users noticed something else.

Boltz had failed to renew its warrant canary—a PGP-signed statement periodically confirming that it had not received secret government demands for user information. The previous canary, published on May 31, promised an update every 60 days, making July 30 the expected renewal date. Instead, the company remained silent for more than five days before publishing a new canary on Aug. 5.

카나리아 새가 죽었다는 뜻이 이거구나, 얘네 지금 기관/정부측으로부터 말 못할 무언가의 명령을 받았다, 그리고 서비스 정지, 공격

지금 일어나는 모든 상황들이 전부 의심스럽습니다 전 https://t.co/gKNuTE7Rjj

— 천우희🔧 #BIP-110 (@uhuiNode) August 5, 2026

Boltz's own warning fueled the panic

The delay immediately raised alarms because of the language Boltz itself had chosen. Its previous warrant canary instructed users to "assume the worst" if the statement was not renewed on schedule.

Within hours, some members of the Bitcoin community began speculating that the company had received a secret subpoena, gag order or other government demand that prevented it from updating the notice.

Bitcoin commentator Adam Simecka described the expired canary as an "authenticated deadman switch," claiming it indicated that a government agency had taken control of Boltz. He later urged users to distrust further communications from the company, suggesting its developers could be operating under duress. Similar concerns also surfaced on Stacker News, where users pointed to the missed deadline as a potential warning signal.

If we can't take warrant canaries seriously, then we don't deserve to be taken seriously ourselves.

FYI, Samourai's canary expired. They dismissed it (under duress). Turned out to be real.

Boltz did the entire Bitcoin space a huge favor. We owe them our gratitude. 🙏 https://t.co/Rz7xoGnozopic.twitter.com/ekern1l9G5

— Adam Simecka (@AdamSimecka) August 6, 2026

Boltz has since renewed the warrant canary using its normal PGP signing key. The updated notice states that the company has received "0 requests for information of any kind by any third parties including but not limited to government agencies." It also contains a recent Bitcoin block hash, matching the format used in previous canary updates.

Supporters of the project argue the controversy resulted from poor timing rather than government intervention. They noted that warrant canaries are updated manually and said the team simply overlooked the deadline while focusing on containing the ongoing security incident.

A reminder that warrant canaries rely on trust

Warrant canaries are designed to alert users if a service can no longer truthfully state that it has avoided secret government demands. Because companies may be legally prohibited from disclosing certain investigations, many choose to periodically publish signed statements confirming that no such requests have been received.

When those statements suddenly stop appearing, users are left to interpret the silence. In Boltz's case, the combination of an indefinite service shutdown, mounting AI-driven attacks and a missed warrant canary renewal transformed a procedural oversight into a full-blown trust crisis.

Although the company now says it has received no government requests, the incident demonstrates how transparency tools intended to build confidence can just as quickly undermine it when they fail at the worst possible moment.

data.title: AI-Powered Bitcoin Red Team Warns Security Is "Extremely Bad" After Finding Thousands of Potential Software Flaws
data.description:
AI Bitcoin Security Sweep Uncovers Thousands of Potential Flaws

A volunteer team of Bitcoin developers and security researchers has uncovered thousands of potential software vulnerabilities after launching an AI-assisted review of open-source Bitcoin projects following the recent Coldcard hardware wallet exploit, which resulted in losses of more than $100 million.

Known as Bitcoin Red Team, the initiative has reviewed more than 390 open-source repositories covering Bitcoin wallets, cryptographic libraries, infrastructure software and other core projects.

The campaign has so far produced 4,962 security findings, including 85 classified as critical and 635 rated as high severity.

The effort is led by Bitcoin developer Calle, creator of the Android version of Bitchat, and AnchorWatch CEO Rob Hamilton, alongside a globally distributed group of 16 volunteers.

The team has spent more than $40,000 on AI computing, with funding provided by OpenSats, a non-profit organisation that supports open-source Bitcoin development.

red teaming bitcoin:

- we’ve written multiple harnesses and we’re launching a huge wave of reviews against many core bitcoin projects: crypto libs, wallets, infra, …
- situation is extremely bad.
- we’re averaging on the order of 1 critical exploit per hour per person.
- we’ve… https://t.co/9zlaaObU03

— calle (@callebtc) August 4, 2026

How AI Is Speeding Up Bitcoin Security Reviews

Rather than relying only on traditional manual audits, the team combines AI models with human verification to examine large amounts of code in a short period of time.

The review uses frontier AI models including Kimi K3, GPT Sol, Fable, Opus and GLM5.2.

The project initially depended heavily on Chinese open-source AI models before expanding to include OpenAI and Anthropic models as access became available.

According to Calle, the campaign has been progressing at an unusually fast pace.

"27.5 hours in, we've filed 4,962 findings across 390 projects. 85 critical and 635 high severity issues. We're at 2.31 h+c findings per person per hour."

Bitcoin Red Team update: we've grown to 16 globally distributed people working 24/7

We're running a large-scale ecosystem security audit across bitcoin code bases.

27.5 hours in, we've filed 4,962 findings across 390 projects. 85 critical and 635 high severity issues.

We're at… pic.twitter.com/iRCylprbY1

— calle (@callebtc) August 5, 2026

In another update, Calle said the group was "averaging on the order of 1 critical exploit per hour per person" and described the overall security situation as "extremely bad."

Not Every Finding Is A Confirmed Vulnerability

Although the number of reported issues is large, the team cautioned that the findings should not all be treated as confirmed exploitable vulnerabilities.

We're ramping up.

Much of our work is still manual (hand holding the AI) but our automated harnesses are getting better at the same time.

So far, letting everyone use their own favorite review method has proven to be the most effective strategy.

We're getting a lot of… pic.twitter.com/EoS6Z9ubpr

— calle (@callebtc) August 5, 2026

Around 21.4% of the reported issues have already been successfully reproduced, meaning those findings have been independently verified.

The remaining reports still require further investigation, as AI-assisted security reviews can generate false positives, duplicate reports or issues that may not be exploitable in real-world conditions.

Critical vulnerabilities are already being disclosed privately to affected open-source projects through a responsible disclosure process before any public release.

Open-Source Security Tools Planned For Wider Use

Alongside identifying vulnerabilities, Bitcoin Red Team plans to release its custom AI security harness as open-source software.

The framework is designed to identify important software libraries, reproduce vulnerabilities, package supporting evidence into reports and help developers coordinate responsible disclosures.

The team said the security harness could also allow Bitcoin companies to test their own closed-source software, extending the same review process beyond public repositories.

Bitcoin's AI red team found 85 critical bugs in about a day

A volunteer effort dubbed the Bitcoin Red Team, led by AnchorWatch CEO Rob Hamilton (@Rob1Ham) and Bitchat developer Calle (@callebtc), has filed nearly 5,000 findings across 390 open source Bitcoin repositories in 27.5… pic.twitter.com/aLAhmcJ8hK

— BSCN (@BSCNews) August 5, 2026

Hamilton said AI remains a tool rather than a replacement for experienced engineers, noting that engineers "...might otherwise 'smell out something is wrong,' but might be missing niche context."

The campaign continues to expand as contributors review more Bitcoin software while seeking additional computing resources and AI access to support the ongoing security effort.

data.title: Ethereum Foundation Seeks AI Researcher to Protect Ethereum From Hidden Threats Across Its Core Infrastructure
data.description:
Ethereum Foundation Expands AI Security Team to Protect Core Protocol

Keeping Ethereum secure is becoming an even bigger priority as the Ethereum Foundation looks to strengthen the team responsible for finding weaknesses before they can affect the network.

The organisation is recruiting an AI-focused Protocol Security Researcher to help identify vulnerabilities across Ethereum's core infrastructure, combining automated security testing with detailed human analysis.

The new role is designed to support the Foundation's Protocol Security team, which reviews critical parts of Ethereum before software updates reach the main network.

Rather than responding to an active security incident, the recruitment is aimed at strengthening long-term protocol security.

🚨 The @ethereumfndn Protocol Security team is hiring!

Come help secure Ethereum mainnet and the next generation of protocol upgrades.

Apply: https://t.co/X0xB7c1e6s

— Nikos (@nikosbaxevanis) August 6, 2026

The Role Covers Every Layer of Ethereum

The successful candidate will investigate security issues across Ethereum's execution layer, which processes transactions and smart contracts, as well as the consensus layer that coordinates validators.

The work also extends to the peer-to-peer network, protocol specifications and the client software responsible for implementing Ethereum's rules.

Responsibilities include developing fuzzing tools, reviewing protocol changes planned for future hard forks, manually auditing updates and coordinating the responsible disclosure of confirmed vulnerabilities.

The Foundation also expects the researcher to use AI systems to automate parts of vulnerability discovery while independently verifying every confirmed finding before it is reported.

Why Human Researchers Still Matter

Although AI is becoming increasingly useful for identifying possible security flaws, the Foundation said human expertise remains essential to determine which findings are genuine.

During recent internal testing, coordinated AI agents examined Ethereum protocol code, cryptographic software and other network components.

The experiments successfully uncovered real software flaws, but researchers found that verifying those discoveries required far more effort than detecting them.

"The agents found real bugs…Agents finding bugs wasn't the surprise. The surprise was how little of the work went into finding them, and how much went into telling the real bugs from the ones that just looked real."

One confirmed issue involved a remotely triggered panic affecting libp2p's gossipsub component, which is used by Ethereum consensus clients for peer-to-peer communication.

Developers fixed the vulnerability before it was publicly disclosed as CVE-2026-34219.

Researchers said every AI-generated report still required reproducible evidence, proof-of-concept code and manual review before it could be classified as a genuine vulnerability.

The Protocol Security Team has been pointing AI agents at Ethereum’s protocol code. Our core takeaway wasn't about finding bugs, it was about triage.

Here are field notes from the work.https://t.co/HVtc8XcrJK

— Ethereum Foundation (@ethereumfndn) July 9, 2026

Experienced Ethereum Engineers Preferred

The Foundation is looking for candidates with deep knowledge of the Ethereum protocol and has indicated that engineers who have already contributed to protocol development or understand execution-layer and consensus-layer specifications will be preferred.

The role involves working with programming languages including Go, Rust, Java, C#, Nim and Python.

It is a remote position open to applicants across Europe and other regions worldwide.

Recruitment Continues After Foundation Restructuring

The vacancy follows a recent restructuring at the Ethereum Foundation that resulted in the closure of its Protocol Support team and the removal of 54 roles, representing about 20% of the organisation's workforce.

🚨 @ethereumfndn Restructures

The @ethereum Foundation has completed a major internal restructuring.

Key updates:

• 54 employees (around 20% of the team) have been laid off
• Lower operating costs could reduce future $ETH selling by the Foundation
• The EF says this is part… https://t.co/ZdOCR7I556pic.twitter.com/NQbb5NMdhc

— Crypto Sunny (@Crypto_SunnyS) June 27, 2026

The former team had coordinated core developer meetings, tracked network upgrades, supported contributors working on Ethereum Improvement Proposals and managed training programmes for new protocol developers.

Since then, several former researchers have moved into independent organisations.

Mo Jalil, Oskar Thorén and Aaryamann Challani launched EthSystems, a commercial company developing confidential Ethereum infrastructure for regulated institutions with backing from Bitmine, SharpLink and Consensys CEO Joe Lubin.

Former Foundation researcher Francesco D'Amato also joined independent protocol research group Ethlabs on 16 July 2026.

Status update: I am moving from the Ethereum Foundation to Ethlabs @ethlabs_org, joining the team to accelerate protocol work in the age of Ethereum adoption.

In 5 years at EF Research, I have worked on research and specification of a wide range of Protocol R&D: mev, consensus,…

— Francesco (@fradamt) July 16, 2026

Despite the broader restructuring, the latest recruitment shows the Foundation continues to invest in specialised security expertise while some development and coordination work moves beyond the organisation itself.

Security Remains A Core Priority

The Foundation has continued reinforcing its security focus in recent weeks.

On 29 July 2026, security researcher Pascal Caversaccio joined its board for an initial one-year voluntary term, expanding the board to four members with an emphasis on security, privacy and censorship resistance.

The Foundation said the latest hiring should not be viewed as a response to a newly discovered vulnerability.

Instead, the position strengthens the team responsible for reviewing future protocol upgrades and identifying security weaknesses before changes are deployed across Ethereum's main network.

data.title: Putin Signs Landmark Crypto Law Opening Regulated Retail Trading In Russia
data.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has signed a landmark cryptocurrency law that, for the first time, establishes a comprehensive legal framework for regulated crypto trading in Russia, opening the market to retail investors while preserving the country's longstanding ban on using digital assets for domestic payments.

Russia legalizes crypto trading with a 98% catch

Putin has signed a law legalizing cryptocurrency trading in Russia from September 1, but only through Central Bank-regulated institutions and only for tokens clearing a $61.5B market cap bar over two years, a filter that currently… pic.twitter.com/clYUnI7rB8

— BSCN (@BSCNews) August 4, 2026

The legislation marks one of Russia's biggest policy shifts toward digital assets, transforming crypto from a largely gray-market activity into a regulated financial sector overseen by the Bank of Russia. Vladimir Putin

Russia opens the door to regulated crypto investing

Under the new framework, Russians will be able to buy and sell cryptocurrencies through licensed exchanges, brokers, custodians, trust managers and digital depositories operating under central bank supervision. While cryptocurrencies are formally recognized as tradable property, they remain prohibited as a means of payment or legal tender within Russia.

Crypto exchange Garantex moves money for criminal gangs, rich Russians and a Hamas-linked terror group, raising questions about the effectiveness of U.S. sanctions https://t.co/4FTFvSBng6

— WSJ Markets (@WSJmarkets) October 13, 2023

Retail investors will be limited to purchasing up to 300,000 rubles worth of approved "most liquid" cryptocurrencies per intermediary each year. The law does not specify which assets will qualify under that category.

Qualified investors, however, will face no investment limits. Both retail and professional investors must pass mandatory suitability assessments before accessing the market, while retail traders may qualify for unrestricted status based on their trading history.

🇷🇺 PUTIN Signed Russia’s Crypto Playbook

Bitcoin, Ethereum & USDT are approved for trading

1- Crypto becomes legal property
2- Licensed exchanges come under Central bank supervision
3- Mining, custody & digital assets are officially regulated
4- Retail investors haveva… pic.twitter.com/RaZj6tjsZp

— CryptoWala (@cryptowalax) August 6, 2026

The legislation also introduces licensing requirements for crypto businesses. Exchanges must join a government registry, maintain a minimum equity base of 15 million rubles and become members of a financial market self-regulatory organization before they can legally operate.

Although Russia is embracing regulated crypto investing, the government continues to prohibit digital assets from being used to pay for goods and services domestically.

However, the law explicitly permits cryptocurrencies to be used in cross-border settlements involving foreign trade contracts between Russian residents and overseas counterparties, reinforcing Moscow's broader effort to reduce reliance on Western financial infrastructure following international sanctions.

Telegram faces terrorism-related cases in both Russia and Australia, Senate negotiators make progress on the CLARITY Act's ethics provisions, and South Korea moves closer to taxing crypto gains starting in 2027.@jennsanasie has what you need to know.

Thank you to @hodlwithLedn… pic.twitter.com/chxWCf3ik8

— CoinDesk (@CoinDesk) July 30, 2026

The measure builds on policies introduced in 2024 that allowed businesses to use cryptocurrencies in international trade as an alternative settlement mechanism.

Landmark reform comes alongside tighter oversight

Most provisions of the legislation will take effect on Sept. 1, 2026, officially launching Russia's regulated crypto market. Rules governing the issuance and circulation of certain digital assets will follow a year later on Sept. 1, 2027, while existing exchanges will have a transition period until March 1, 2027 to comply with the new licensing regime.

LATEST: 🇷🇺Russia will legalize crypto trading on September 1 -- but only through Central Bank-regulated institutions.

The reported framework also sets a $61.5B market-cap threshold for eligible tokens, making this regulated access rather than a broad retail opening. pic.twitter.com/VMCroYgWsn

— 𝚀ꜰꜱ ᴅᴀɪʟʏ ɴᴇᴡꜱ ʟɪᴠᴇ (@qfsdailynews) August 6, 2026

The law follows months of regulatory work by the Bank of Russia, which recently published draft rules for organized digital asset trading and requirements for licensed exchanges and digital depositories.

At the same time, Russian authorities continue tightening oversight of other parts of the crypto industry. Last month, the government prohibited cryptocurrency mining and participation in mining pools across Moscow, the surrounding Moscow region and parts of the Kursk region from Aug. 15 through the end of 2032, citing pressure on the country's electricity grid.

Together, the measures reflect Russia's evolving crypto strategy: bringing digital asset trading under direct government supervision while restricting activities that authorities view as posing financial or infrastructure risks.
